title: The Two Ways to Sell AI: Lighthouse or Landgrab?

reader_summary.headline: AI founders must choose between selling to famous companies or finding customers with ready budgets.
reader_summary.overview: The episode explains two sales paths for AI companies: the 'Lighthouse' strategy using famous clients for proof. Founders should pick the approach that fits their current stage and execute quickly rather than overthinking strategy.

key_points.text: Founders should choose between selling to famous companies for proof or finding customers with existing budgets to grow quickly.
key_points.evidence_quote: Do you win a handful of high-profile customers and use their credibility to unlock a market? Or do you find customers with existing budgets, prove the math and capture as much of the market as quickly as possible?

key_points.text: A 'Land Grab' strategy works when you show customers your solution is better and cheaper than what they are currently using.
key_points.evidence_quote: you can kind of come in there and show like the and buyer the math of hey my solution is better than whatever solution you're using today

key_points.text: Harvey is a 'lighthouse' example because it won over top law firms first to prove safety to buyers.
key_points.evidence_quote: when they won the first kind of you know few critical lighthouse accounts inside of their market like that proved traveled like big time and and then you know the buyers that had like this tremendous amount of exposure realized hey it's actually safe from you to buy this

key_points.text: Stewart is a 'land grab' example because it used AI to prove it could collect money better than humans.
key_points.evidence_quote: we have the math to prove it we will be more effective than your current solution in your current human teams at collecting and this will do xyz4 you know improving working capital by a tremendous amount

key_points.text: Founders should spend 99% of their time executing and talking to customers instead of overthinking whether to use a 'lighthouse' or 'landgrab' sales strategy.
key_points.evidence_quote: spend like 1% of your time on the strategy pick it and then spend 99% of your time to execute yeah so you know rather than sit back and say well you know should we do light house or should we land grab get out talk to your customers

thesis: The speakers argue that AI founders must choose between two competing go-to-market strategies: the 'Lighthouse' playbook, which targets high-profile customers in regulated industries to gain social proof, and the 'Land Grab' playbook, which targets customers with existing budgets to prove the math and capture market share quickly. They propose a framework using buyer exposure and proof travel to evaluate which strategy is appropriate for a specific market opportunity.
